newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber market slow on currency attacks.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber market slow on currency attacks.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market was quiet on Wednesday with most players cautious about making any deals because of the pounding taken by regional currencies, dealers said.

"Several people are a bit reluctant to do anything with the situation still unsettled because of all the currency problems in Indonesia and Thailand. That's the reason why it was so quiet in the market this morning," a dealer said.
Traders said thin dealings in the Japanese market kept most of the trade sitting on the sidelines and they will probably wait for leads before making a move in the afternoon session.
"We're really looking to the afternoon more. Some buying may come up then. It was very, very quiet this morning," another trader said.
The major consumers were not seen making offers in the market, dealers said.
At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 91.50 U.S. cents a kg from 92.00 cents.
September RSS1 was indicated at 133.50 Singapore cents (91 U.S. cents) a kg from 134.50 cents.
October TSR20 was seen at 97.75 U.S. cents a kg from 98.25 cents. -- (S$1.46 = US$1) - Rene Pastor (65-870-3085)
